structured_output.reasoning: The incident's frustrated message ("This is bogus: the checks were skipped.") is verbatim one of the six evidence quotes (incident_id 21) the proposal cites as backing this remedy cluster. The failure mode is precisely: agent claimed a check/fix was complete without having run it. The remedy broadens the existing "Fake Release Discipline" claude-md rule into a general "Verification Before Completion Claims" rule that explicitly states: never claim a fix/change/check passed without having executed it first, covering releases, bug fixes, lint/validation runs, and any completion claim generally. This directly targets the exact failure pattern (skipped checks reported as done) rather than a tangential concern. It is a standing, unconditional instruction placed in global CLAUDE.md, which is the standard mitigation mechanism for this class of behavioral-drift incident. No material gap is evident — the rule's scope explicitly includes "validation/lint/test check," which matches the incident's "checks were skipped" framing.
